"Score the card 1-5 on each criterion. For each score give ref, the card line (card:<field>) that decides it, or plan:<field path> when no card line carries it, and a reason of at most 25 words. Use NA only where a criterion allows it. Then name decides_by: the id of the earliest phase after which decision_rule can be applied whichever outcome occurs, or \"none\". A phase that only reproduces a published number, or only measures throughput the question does not ask about, does not count. Give decides_by_reason in at most 25 words. Decide only from the text below; do not use tools.
Root question: Can one long sequential simulation, like a single MCMC chain or a rainfall-runoff model stepped through decades of daily rainfall, be parallelised over time by guessing the whole trajectory and then correcting every step at once with Newton iterations, and does that only work when the system forgets its past? Is compute a major blocker at some level, and could that be fixed with a shit ton of GPU parallelism?
Option record: {\"id\":\"Linear feature representation -> parallel-in-time for free\",\"title\":\"SAE features give the linear basis that triggers the framer's no-forgetting parallel-in-time exception\",\"summary\":\"If the residual-stream trajectory is a linear combination of sparse features, the per-step feature transition is (approximately) linear and x_T = A^T x_0 is computable in O(log T) depth by repeated squaring / diagonalisation (the framer's ParaDiag exception), with no forgetting needed. Goodfire-style SAEs supply the linear decomposition; the open question is whether the feature-to-feature transition is stable enough to compose out of order.\",\"root_link\":\"It bears on the 'can a long sequential simulation be parallelised over time by guessing and correcting' clause: it is the one regime where the answer is yes without needing the system to forget.\",\"compute_open\":\"More parallel compute buys more models, layers, and features analysed to test feature-level linearity; published evidence stops at linear representations of concepts in LLaMA-2 7B (https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.03658) and SAE decompositions of up to 34M features on one middle layer of Claude 3 Sonnet (https://transformer-circuits.pub/2024/scaling-monosemanticity/); unknown above that is whether the residual stream's feature-to-feature transition is linear and time-invariant across all layers and long contexts.\",\"sequential\":\"none: checking linearity is a per-feature regression/probe fit that is independent across features, layers, and models, so it already splits into parallel pieces with no step waiting on another.\",\"source_urls\":[\"https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.03658\",\"https://transformer-circuits.pub/2024/scaling-monosemanticity/\",\"https://www.unige.ch/~gander/siamtoc3.php\"]}
Card:
card:question: Can SAE feature coordinates make a transformer's layer-to-layer transition linear enough to compose out of order by repeated squaring, giving parallel-in-time depth [s_pdiag]?
card:hypothesis: If residual-stream layers are near-linear in SAE features, repeated squaring composes the trajectory in O(log T) depth with no forgetting [s_pdiag].
card:sequential_part: None: each per-feature linearity fit is independent of the others, so no answer waits step after step.
card:method: none
card:if_lever: Composed out-of-order prediction reconstructs at least 90% of true activations at all 42 layers, so the linear ParaDiag shortcut holds.
card:if_not: Composed prediction falls below 90% reconstruction and decays with depth, so residual nonlinearity breaks out-of-order composition.
card:test_summary: Fit per-layer linear feature transitions (Gemma 2 9B, Gemma Scope SAEs), compose them out of order by repeated squaring, and score against the sequential forward pass; compare with the published adjacent-layer transport R² of 0.95 [s_ato].
card:closest_prior: Prior work (Activation Transport Operators) measured per-feature R² of linear layer-to-layer maps up to a 10-layer leap on a small open model, in under 50 GPU-hours [s_ato].
card:left_open: It did not compose operators out of order over full depth, sweep SAE width, or test time-invariance across contexts on a production-scale model.
card:anchor: SAE encoder-decoder round-trip reproduces released weights to relative error under 1e-5; composition code matches sequential on a synthetic linear system.
card:limits: Holds for open Gemma/LLaMA models and released SAEs, not Claude 3 Sonnet's 34M features; it measures linearity, not a shipped parallel sampler.

Criteria:
stakes: Take the two outcomes this test predicts, as measured here and within the limits in scope_gap. 5 = whichever occurs, a choice someone faces (what to buy, build, collect or scale next) changes, and the test measures the quantity that choice depends on; 3 = the outcomes bear on that choice only through a step this test does not check (a stand-in system, simulation to reality, a single model), or one outcome is already much more likely than the other; 1 = neither outcome would change anything. Do not score how famous the field is or how close it is to the root question.
lever: Could the result tell if_lever from if_not, with compute the only thing that changed? Check four conditions: (a) the predicted difference between if_lever and if_not is larger than what noise_rule says run-to-run noise can produce; (b) compute_axis spans at least 10×; (c) the varied quantity is bought with compute, not with more data, labels or people (when restructuring.method is not none: the arms run on the same hardware and differ only in method); (d) inputs that could also explain the difference are in held_fixed. 5 = all four hold; 3 = one fails or cannot be told from the plan; 1 = two or more fail, or the measured quantity is not the one the question asks about.
verifiable: What is the measured outcome scored against? 5 = an exact or planted truth that does not come from the method under test (a simulation's hidden true run, an exact success flag, a formal checker, planted items), and the setup first reproduces a published number within a stated tolerance; 3 = labels from a model or human rater with an agreement check, or exact truth with no reproduction step; 1 = nothing independent of the method's own output.
open: Does the closest published result already answer this question over this range? 5 = the quoted prior stops short of this range or asks a different question, and the plan states the gap; 3 = the prior answers part of it (a narrower range, a related system), or no prior is named; 1 = the quoted prior already answers it. Reusing published tools, models or benchmarks does not lower this score.
internals: Does the test compare the internals readout with the strongest outputs-only method named in the plan or the option, on the same items, with a numeric margin in decision_rule? 5 = yes; 3 = compares only with a weaker outputs-only method than one named, or gives no margin; 1 = no outputs-only comparison.
reshape: Does the plan remove a step-after-step dependency that one answer waits on, rather than run independent work side by side? 5 = restructuring names the dependency, why it need not run in order and how the plan computes it at the same time; condition says what must hold for that to pay off; condition_phase measures it before the main spend; and the closest prior does not already do this for this system; 3 = it removes a dependency, but condition is missing or is not measured before the main spend; 2 = it parallelises only within each step (splitting a large state across GPUs) or regroups and rebalances independent work (batching unfinished runs, load balancing, lower precision), leaving the chain in order; 1 = independent copies side by side, or one job per GPU, is the only parallelism, or the plan rebuilds a parallel version the closest prior already reports for this system. Reusing a method published for a different system does not lower this score.
baseline: Is the gain timed against the strongest ways to get the same answer without the plan's method? Check four conditions: (a) baseline_sequential is tuned (compiled, vectorised or multithreaded code, or a published optimised code), not a plain interpreted loop; (b) baseline_copies is timed on the same GPUs; (c) anchor checks the parallel result against the sequential one within a stated tolerance; (d) a named phase times every arm as time or dollars to one answer, so the gain is measured, not only modelled. 5 = all four hold; 3 = one fails or cannot be told from the plan; 1 = two or more fail. NA when restructuring.method is none.

Let me carefully score this card against each criterion.

The card is about testing whether SAE feature coordinates make transformer layer-to-layer transitions linear enough to compose out of order by repeated squaring, giving parallel-in-time depth.

**stakes**: The two outcomes are if_lever (composed out-of-order prediction reconstructs ≥90% of true activations at all 42 layers) and if_not (falls below 90% and decays with depth). Within the limits in scope_gap (Gemma/LLaMA, not Claude 3 Sonnet 34M, measures linearity not shipped sampler), does a choice someone faces change?

If the result is if_lever, it suggests SAE features give a linear basis enabling ParaDiag-style parallel-in-time composition without forgetting - a major architectural finding. If if_not, then residual nonlinearity breaks out-of-order composition, so parallel-in-time via this route doesn't work for transformers.

These outcomes bear on the root question about whether long sequential simulations can be parallelised by guessing/correcting, specifically whether SAE features trigger the "no-forgetting" exception. The test measures linearity R² which is the quantity that matters for this choice.

However, scope_gap notes it doesn't transfer to proprietary models and doesn't test a shipped parallel sampler. So one outcome is more impactful than the other but both still bear on the choice.
